analysis.title: Broadcom Inc. (AVGO): 3Q Preview: Expect modest upside, with focus on AI revenue outlook, datacenter visibility, and ASIC competition
key_insights: GS keeps a Buy on AVGO and cuts the 12-month price target from $540 to $460. The target is 25X (down from 30X on lower peer multiples) normalized EPS of $18.00, which is unchanged. Against the $341.60 price this implies 34.7% upside.
GS expects modest upside to FY4Q26 and FY1Q27 results and guidance. Its FY27 and FY28 AI revenue estimates are 5% and 9% above Street, and its EPS estimates are 5% and 12% above.

Expectations are described as muted heading into the print because visibility on the durability of AI spending is limited and land, power and shell constraints are intensifying into 2028. They have improved somewhat after the stock's outperformance over the past week.

First call focus is FY27 AI guidance. Emerging hyperscalers account for about 6.3GW of Broadcom's roughly 10GW of FY27 custom XPU deployments, so external funding is the main investor concern. Added visibility that reaffirms FY27 shipments could be impactful.

Second focus is customer readiness for FY28. Emerging hyperscalers are about 75% of planned FY28 XPU deployments. Any visibility that partially de-risks the 20 GW FY28 target could be a meaningful catalyst, given investor scrutiny of land, power, shell and funding since the midterm elections.

Third focus is competition. GS wants detail on the durability of key customer engagements for next-generation XPUs as competitive intensity rises from providers such as MediaTek, and on Broadcom's share position at key XPU customers including Google.
GS expects the stock to be driven more by clarity on AI spending sustainability into 2028 and Broadcom's competitive position at key accounts such as Google than by the quarterly beat itself.
GS is above Street on FY27 and FY28 revenue (2% and 6%) and operating income (3% and 9%). Its FY28 gross margin is 71 bps above Street and its FY28 operating margin is 176 bps above.
The segment mix differs from Street. GS is above on AI Semis for FY27 and FY28 (+5%, +9%) and below on Non-AI Semis (-5%, -7%) and Infrastructure Software (-3%, -4%).
For FY1Q27 the GS AI Semis estimate is 2% below Street (24,096 vs 24,638) while Non-AI Semis and Infrastructure Software are above Street.

market_movers.rationale: GS cuts the target from $540 to $460 on a lower 25X multiple (from 30X) applied to unchanged normalized EPS of $18.00. It expects modest upside to guidance and estimates above Street on FY27 and FY28 AI revenue.

earnings_insights: FY4Q26E, GS estimates (not reported): revenue $35,041mn vs Street estimate $34,876mn, EPS excl. SBC $3.91 vs Street estimate $3.84. AI Semis revenue $21,906mn vs Street estimate $21,719mn.
FY1Q27E guidance and estimates, GS vs Street estimate: revenue $37,406mn vs $37,528mn, EPS excl. SBC $4.26 vs $4.14, AI Semis $24,096mn vs $24,638mn.
FY2027E, GS estimates vs Street estimate: revenue $177,004mn vs $173,639mn, EPS excl. SBC $20.20 vs $19.17, AI Semis $125,477mn vs $119,129mn.
FY2028E, GS estimates vs Street estimate: revenue $294,374mn vs $278,498mn, EPS excl. SBC $34.25 vs $30.62, AI Semis $240,306mn vs $220,712mn.
GS expects modest upside to FY4Q/FY1Q results and guidance. The print itself had not happened as of this 18 November 2026 note.
risk_factors: Share loss in the custom compute franchise.
Persistent inventory digestion in non-AI semiconductors.
External funding for emerging hyperscalers, which are a growing share of XPU shipments.
FY28 land, power and shell availability constraints.
Competitive intensity at key XPU accounts such as Google from providers including MediaTek.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects modest upside to guidance and has FY27 and FY28 AI revenue 5% and 9% above Street. Incremental visibility on FY27 shipments or the 20 GW FY28 target could be a meaningful catalyst.
tension_points.bear_case: Land, power and shell constraints are intensifying into 2028, and external funding for emerging hyperscalers is uncertain. These customers are about 6.3GW of ~10GW of FY27 XPU deployments and about 75% of planned FY28 deployments.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Management failing to reaffirm FY27 shipments to emerging hyperscalers, or failing to de-risk any part of the 20 GW FY28 target, on the call.
